one_liner: Yann Collet's standalone tANS (FSE) and 4-stream Huffman (Huff0) block coders, the entropy stage later built into zstd.
what_it_does: A C library of two block entropy coders over byte alphabets: FSE, a table-based asymmetric numeral systems (tANS) coder, and Huff0, a Huffman coder. The simple API is FSE_compress/FSE_decompress and HUF_compress/HUF_decompress on caller-allocated buffers, returning a size or an error code tested with FSE_isError/HUF_isError; a detailed API exposes counting, normalization, table build and per-table encode/decode so a format can reuse tables. It is not a drop-in for zlib: there is no stream or container format, and the caller stores block sizes and handles raw/RLE blocks (FSE_decompress does not decode them; HUF_decompress needs the exact original size).
how_it_is_fast: FSE is Jarek Duda's tANS: symbol probabilities are normalized to a power of two (2^tableLog, default 2^13 table) and each symbol becomes one table lookup plus a variable bit read or write, with no multiplication or division; the decoder runs two interleaved states over one bitstream so the CPU overlaps their dependency chains. Huff0 splits each block into four independently decodable streams behind a jump table and decodes them in one loop for instruction-level parallelism, with single-symbol (X1) and double-symbol (X2) lookup tables limited to 11-12 bits and an optional BMI2 code path. Both use a 64-bit branch-light bit container (bitstream.h) that refills with unaligned word loads.
when_to_use: You are building your own compressor format and need an order-0 entropy stage after LZ, BWT or transform coding, with per-block (up to 128 KB for Huff0) static statistics
Skewed byte distributions where Huffman's 1-bit-per-symbol floor costs ratio: FSE reached 8.84x on Proba80 versus 6.38x for Huff0 and zlibh
Flat or moderately skewed data where decode speed matters more than the last percent of ratio: Huff0 decoded 2.9-4.5x faster than zlibh in the README tests
You want to study or prototype with the upstream reference of the coders inside zstd, in a small set of files that compile independently for compression or decompression
when_not_to_use: Untrusted input or fuzz-exposed services: four open memory-safety reports from 2025-2026 (#121 heap write overflow in FSE_compress_usingCTable on single-symbol input, #122 stack underflow in FSE_compress2, #123 segfault in FSE_decompress_usingDTable on a 6-byte round trip, #124 1-byte out-of-bounds write in HUF_decompress4X1 when dstSize is small and not a multiple of 4) have no maintainer reply

Production use where you can take zstd instead: zstd's lib/common and lib/compress carry the maintained, fuzzed copies of the same FSE and Huff0 code, while this repo's library code has had no functional change since 2020
Peak entropy-decode throughput on current CPUs: later SIMD rANS and Huffman decoders (hypersonic-rANS, htscodecs, PIVCO-Huffman) report several times FSE's and Huff0's decode speed
Alphabets above 256 symbols with Huff0 (HUF_SYMBOLVALUE_MAX 255); FSE has a separate fseU16 variant, with an open clipping bug (#97)
Adaptive or context-mixing models: both coders assume one static distribution per block, sent as a header

integration.dependencies: none (libc malloc/free only for the create/free table helpers; workspace variants avoid allocation)
integration.min_toolchain: C89-compatible with C99 stdint.h used when available; a 2024 PR updated the programs/ build for current compilers; README benchmark used GCC 4.8.4
integration.platforms: any; little- and big-endian handled through MEM_isLittleEndian; BMI2 decode path on x86-64 when enabled; GitHub Actions builds all supported platforms
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; functions work on caller-supplied tables, buffers and workspaces with no global state seen in the sources, so separate contexts per thread is the safe assumption

gotchas: Return value 0 means incompressible (nothing written) and FSE_compress returns 1 for single-symbol input (use RLE); FSE_decompress cannot decode either case, so your format must flag them
HUF_decompress needs the exact original size, and HUF_compress rejects blocks larger than 128 KB
Everything under HUF_STATIC_LINKING_ONLY / FSE_STATIC_LINKING_ONLY (table sizes, workspace and X1/X2 APIs) is marked unstable and not for dynamic libraries
lib/ is dual BSD-2-Clause or GPLv2 at your option, but the programs/ benchmark and fuzzer tools are GPLv2 only
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it when you need a portable, plain-C pair of block coders with a precise tANS option and no SIMD requirement, or the upstream reference for zstd's entropy stage; for raw decode speed hypersonic-rANS (enwik8 decode about 3.1x FSE) and PIVCO-Huffman (5.9x huf0 X2 on Apple M4 Max) win, and htscodecs gives a maintained interleaved rANS library.
verified_claims_summary: On an Intel Core i7-5600U (Linux Mint, GCC 4.8.4, 64-bit, flags not stated; the programs Makefile defaults to -O3), the author's README splits probagen-generated files into 32 KB blocks: Huff0 decodes 1350/860/555 MB/s on Proba80/14/02 versus zlibh's 300/250/210 MB/s and encodes 600/595/525 versus 265/255/180 MB/s, while FSE runs 325-330 MB/s encode and 440-460 MB/s decode with the best ratio on Proba80. The baseline is zlib's Huffman stage as packaged by Frederic Kayser, on synthetic data only.
status_note: Stale: the last commits (March 2024) touched only CI and the benchmark build, the library code last synced with zstd in 2020, and four memory-safety issues are unanswered; BSD-2-Clause library code is easy to vendor, but take zstd's copy for anything exposed to untrusted data.
